instructions: Fill in every null 'human' field with one of the labels listed under 'labels', judging each item from the question, the cited passages and the answer only (not from your own knowledge of the FOMC). claims: is the claim supported by the cited passages taken together (supported), contradicted by one of them, or neither (unsupported)? A different holder (Committee, members, participants, staff), a stronger or weaker quantifier, or a different number or date is not supported. citations: does passage [n] support the quoted text its marker is attached to (supports), some of its claims (partially_supports), or none (does_not_support)? facts: does the answer state the required fact (covered), state something incompatible (contradicted), or neither (missing)? response_type: does the answer answer the question (answers), answer part of it and say what is missing (partial), or say the passages do not answer it (declines)? The judge's verdicts are in a separate key file: do not open it before you finish. Save the filled file as rag_judge_annotations.json next to this one.
annotator: three Claude Opus 5.5 sessions, not people: C, isolated (it saw only a copy of the sample), and A and B, two earlier sessions whose independence cannot be verified

C vs A measures it: 376 of 383 labels agree. All three are the same model, so judge vs annotator compares gpt-5.5 with Claude, not with a person.
